title: IO-Link (IEC 61131-9 SDCI) master port or device data link layer: wake-up, M-sequences with PD / OD, checksums, 256-byte message buffer

device: reply delay in bit times after the middle of the last stop bit (0 acts as 1)
PCLK cycles per bit, >= 4 (217 = COM3 at 50 MHz)
PCLK cycles of the wake-up request (80 us at 50 MHz); a device accepts +-1/16

regs.desc: Octet counts and master reply timeout

fields.desc: master: bit times of silence before a timeout
{R/W (1 read), channel (0 process, 1 page, 2 diagnosis, 3 ISDU), address}

regs.desc: Message buffer address for CMD.host_rd / host_wr

features: Master port: wake-up request, M-sequences of any type with 0..32 PD octets each way and 0..32 OD octets, reply timeout, checksum, parity and framing checks
Device: wake-up detection (+-1/16), frame checks with reports, 16-bit-time drop after errors, programmable reply delay, page channel served from a 32-octet parameter page
UART 8E1 at any bit time from 4 PCLK cycles (COM1 / COM2 / COM3), 256 x 8 message buffer
notes: txd / tx_en drive the C/Q transceiver, rxd is the received line (1 idle); the line is ignored while tx_en is high.
Not implemented: ISDU segmentation, event memory and the startup / preoperate state machines (host software uses the channels directly).
sequence: Master: CTRL.cfg_master = 1, TIMING, LENGTHS; CMD.m_wurq, then for each cycle write the PD out / OD octets, MC, CMD.m_start; on IRQ M_DONE read M_STATUS and the reply at 0x40 / 0x60.
Device: CTRL, TIMING, LENGTHS; keep PD in at 0x00, OD at 0x20 and the page at 0x80; on IRQ D_MSG_AVAIL read D_MSG and the received octets at 0x40 / 0x60.
